The gaps, each verified in the code: a declared host that has not been the right one since the migration, hence a declared transfer outside the European Union that does not exist and the real processor omitted; private chat messages not declared at all, the feature having arrived after the document's last update; Discord declared nowhere even though accepted crash reports are sent there by webhook and hosted in the United States; the Steam avatar over-declared, nothing storing it server-side; and GDPR rights pointed at an email address while export and deletion are already self-service in the game.

The Cookies section was flatly wrong, and it is the only point the previous correction had left untouched. It claimed "a session cookie only" and "no analytics tracker is used at this time", while page-view tracking is mounted on every page of the site and the API sets a one-year visitor cookie on the first visit. The cookie itself is clean, and that is what makes the correction simple: a random identifier, never an IP address, no cross-referencing with any other processing, a purpose limited to measurement, and twelve months, hence under the thirteen-month ceiling of the French regulator's audience-measurement exemption. No consent banner to add: this was a sentence to rewrite, not a feature to restrict.

Last point, and the most interesting technically: two tables had been missed by account deletion ever since they were created. The function lists its tables by hand and nothing tied that list to the schema, so two tables added after the GDPR rights were written were neither erased nor exported. The real impact is small, the Steam id going first, so whatever survives is no longer attributable to anyone, but it is a silent omission bound to repeat with every new table. The useful fix is not the two deletions added, it is the guard: a test reads the database schema and requires every table with a foreign key to accounts to be either erased or listed as deliberately retained with its reason. A new table therefore fails the suite until someone decides, and written before the fix, it flagged exactly those two tables.

Two follow-ups stay open, and they are contract text to arbitrate, not code. The terms of sale open with "Wyrdane offers no real-money purchases" while card backs have been on sale since 13 November. And the data export does not return nine tables that deletion nonetheless erases: defensible, but that is article 15 rather than 17, so it deserves an explicit decision.

en.heading: The companion site
paragraphs: A lot of work on the site, and it starts with an embarrassing defect on a public site. The site's card data was stale: 228 cards against 304 in the game. The whole Human race was missing, 76 cards plus its resource card, so the web deck builder simply could not build a Human deck. And a renamed card still appeared under its old name, the same rename never propagated, in a third place. Resynchronised, with the card text translation table regenerated in the same pass, 1863 entries.

French name casing was ported to the site, reusing the game's function: "Brise-Mort de Skeldara" displays as "Brise-mort de Skeldara". For display only, the name remaining the key that links to the server.

The home page changed in nature. The three explorers, card types, keywords and triggers, no longer show one hand-written example card but every real card concerned, in a carousel that scrolls in an endless loop. Cards scroll in black and white and regain their colours on hover, with the scrolling pausing meanwhile: without that, the coloured card escapes the cursor before it can be read. The demo texts that re-explained the example card's effect disappeared along with the hand-written file that carried them, 1002 lines less.

The site's card data generator now outputs each card's artwork and triggers, read straight from the game's resources. Trap found there: the engine does not write a field left at its default value, so a trigger with no type counted as Last Breath, and eight cards were invisible in the tally. A verification script now refuses to let a home page entry end up with an empty carousel.

The site's card was realigned on the game's: a single border shared by the four races instead of one per race, darkened as in game, the black frame tightened accordingly, the type banner dropped in favour of the medallion that carries rarity, the medallion logo tinted, and lane icons switched to the white variants. A technical detail along the way: the site's image copies were indexed PNGs, which had crushed the frame's soft transparency and turned the icons grey-blue. Re-copied as RGBA from the game, and one image instead of four, 381 KB down to 199.

Finally, the Journal of Aldrenia now reads properly on a phone. Two defects stacked: the page-flip library set minimum sizes larger than the book itself, so the page block overflowed 52 pixels past the right of the screen, and all the typography is computed as a proportion of page width on a ratio tuned for the desktop double page, far too large for a phone page where height is the constraint. Measured on the first pages of the three volumes: up to 123% overflow before, 0% after.

en.heading: A comfort pass
paragraphs: A run of small things with nothing in common except having been noticed while playing. Stat changes shown as floating text above a minion are emphasised, because it is combat's most useful information and it went unnoticed. The Match found prompt now sits in a gold panel like the rest of the interface, and no longer takes keyboard focus on tab, where it stole the navigation. On the versus screen, the hero artwork is smaller and the vertical rank text is fixed.

Three more: tooltip panels became fully transparent to the mouse, having intercepted clicks meant for what lay underneath; the quests' New players tab shows as soon as the view opens instead of waiting for a refresh; and on the deck side, a tile's artwork is shown uncropped in 2:3 with the tile itself tightened, while in the deck builder the buy button moved to the top of the card and the layout now stays stable when you add a card you do not own, which it did not.

en.heading: Tidying up
paragraphs: Three weeks of work leave a mess behind, and part of those three weeks went into clearing it. The project documentation was split up: the main context file weighed 177 KB, and every session paid to load all of it for sections consulted once in twenty. The two other large files had the same flaw, you had to load them whole to find one keyword definition or one card. Everything was spread into appendices, one per subject, without losing anything.

On the code side, dead code removed, and about thirty files whose comment blocks of nine lines or more were condensed, up to 38 lines for the longest. The rule applied: keep the why and the invariants, drop the dated historical narrative, which already lives in the documentation.

And the effect engine, 1949 lines, had its targeting, thresholds and execution conditions extracted into a separate 270-line file, all static and stateless. The engine drops to 1690 lines, three facades staying in place for calls coming from other systems, so no caller changed. Two adjacency functions were in fact each other's body word for word, a copy rather than a variant: merged.
One last unrelated fix that deserved its line: the combat log froze the game past 200 entries.

A technical debt review closed the file for good, with two useful conclusions. The only code debt still open, a discard we believed was never announced to the network peer, was a false positive: the peer replays the trigger itself and recounts its own hand, so sending a discard command on top would have removed the card twice on their side and created the opposite drift, that one real. The effect was covered by no test at all, which is exactly why nobody had seen it: three tests now pin it, the local hand size, the absence of a network command, and the opponent's counter left unchanged. Noted along the way and deliberately not fixed: the repository cleanup done in September has regressed, 49 worktrees mounted and 82 local branches against 4 and 7 after the cleanup. Recorded rather than done blind, because sessions may be working inside those copies.
The test suite went from 953 to 1156 tests across 104 scripts, all green.

en.heading: What's next
paragraphs: The watch item from Devlog 13 has not moved: the new player. Quests only pay for matchmade multiplayer, solo pays nothing, and the tutorial and starter decks lead precisely into solo first. The playtest review adds to it: there is no way to skip the tutorial, and the anti-AFK guard cuts turns in solo.

The freeze is still open, but no longer blind: the watchdog captured its first trace and the search is down to a short window. What is missing is the native stack, so a memory dump taken during a freeze, and a session that freezes on an exported build rather than from the editor, since all four known freezes happened when launching from the editor.

And the beta is getting closer: the build is back to a shippable size, the version finally displays, the starter decks work for all four races. What remains is the twenty-one achievements to enter in Steamworks, the microtransaction publisher key to generate, and the two-real-Steam-account test that networked Arena and direct rendezvous are both still waiting on.
